sn35.94:1.2: “Bhikkhus, these six bases for contact—if untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained—are bringers of suffering.
sn35.94:1.4: “The eye, bhikkhus, as a base for contact—if untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained—is a bringer of suffering.
sn35.94:1.5: The ear as a base for contact …
sn35.94:1.6: The mind as a base for contact … is a bringer of suffering.
sn35.94:1.7: These six bases for contact—if untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained—are bringers of suffering.
sn35.94:2.1: “Bhikkhus, these six bases for contact—if well tamed, well guarded, well protected, well restrained—are bringers of happiness.
sn35.94:2.3: “The eye, bhikkhus, as a base for contact—if well tamed, well guarded, well protected, well restrained—is a bringer of happiness.
sn35.94:2.4: The ear as a base for contact …
sn35.94:2.5: The mind as a base for contact … is a bringer of happiness.
sn35.94:2.6: These six bases for contact—if well tamed, well guarded, well protected, well restrained—are bringers of happiness.”
sn35.94:2.7: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn35.94:2.8: Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:
sn35.94:3.1: “Just six, O bhikkhus, are the bases for contact,
sn35.94:3.2: Where one unrestrained meets with suffering.
sn35.94:3.3: Those who know how to restrain them
sn35.94:3.4: Dwell uncorrupted, with faith their partner.
sn35.94:4.1: “Having seen forms that delight the mind
sn35.94:4.2: And having seen those that give no delight,
sn35.94:4.3: Dispel the path of lust towards the delightful
sn35.94:4.4:
And do not soil the mind by thinking,
‘The other is displeasing to me.’
sn35.94:5.1: “Having heard sounds both pleasant and raucous,
sn35.94:5.2: Do not be enthralled with pleasant sound.
sn35.94:5.3: Dispel the course of hate towards the raucous,
sn35.94:5.4:
And do not soil the mind by thinking,
‘This one is displeasing to me.’
sn35.94:6.2: And having smelt a putrid stench,
sn35.94:6.4: And do not yield to desire for the lovely.
sn35.94:7.2: And having sometimes tasted what is bitter,
sn35.94:7.3: Do not greedily enjoy the sweet taste,
sn35.94:7.4: Do not feel aversion towards the bitter.
sn35.94:8.1: “When touched by pleasant contact do not be enthralled,
sn35.94:8.2: Do not tremble when touched by pain.
sn35.94:8.3: Look evenly on both the pleasant and painful,
sn35.94:8.4: Not drawn or repelled by anything.
sn35.94:9.2: Perceive and proliferate they become engaged.
sn35.94:9.3: Having dispelled every mind-state bound to the home life,
sn35.94:9.4: One travels on the road of renunciation.
sn35.94:10.1: “When the mind is thus well developed in six,
sn35.94:10.2: If touched, one’s mind never flutters anywhere.
sn35.94:10.3: Having vanquished both lust and hate, O bhikkhus,
sn35.94:10.4: Go to the far shore beyond birth and death!”
